explanation: An Israelite military commander who was anointed king of Israel by God's command to destroy the house of Ahab and Jezebel.
The act of applying oil to someone, often to consecrate them for a special service or position, in this case as king.
The seventh king of Israel who ruled from Samaria and was married to Jezebel. He is known for his idolatry and injustice.
Queen of Israel, wife of King Ahab. She was known for her wickedness, idolatry, and persecution of God's prophets.
A person who receives messages from God and delivers them to the people. Prophets played an important role in Israel's history.
An Israelite who owned a vineyard next to Ahab's palace. Ahab wanted to buy the vineyard, but Nabot refused. Jezebel then conspired to have him killed so that Ahab could take the vineyard.
A city in northern Israel where much of the action in 2 Kings 9 takes place, including the killings of Joram, Ahaziah, and Jezebel.
Son of Ahab and Jezebel; he was king of Israel before Jehu was anointed king and killed him.
King of Judah who was related to Ahab and Jezebel through his mother Athaliah. He was also killed by Jehu.
God's righteous punishment for sin and evil, especially in relation to the family of Ahab and Jezebel as a result of their idolatry and wickedness.
